## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical knowledge of implementing secure credential rotation for SAP HANA deployments in AWS, ensuring adherence to security best practices and automation principles.

## Key Concepts
- AWS Secrets Manager rotation lifecycle for SAP credentials
- SAP HANA SQL commands for user password management
- IAM role design with cross-service permissions and least privilege
- Infrastructure as Code using CloudFormation for reproducible deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  SAPSecret:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    Properties:
      Name: sap/prod/hana
      Description: "SAP HANA production credentials"
      GenerateSecretString:
        SecretStringTemplate: '{"username":"sapadm"}'
        GenerateStringKey: "password"
        PasswordLength: 32
        ExcludeCharacters: '"@/\'
      RotationRule:
        AutomaticallyAfterDays: 30
        RotationLambdaARN: !GetAtt SAPRotationFunction.Arn
  SAPRotationFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: SAPHANA-Rotation
      Runtime: python3.9
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Role: !GetAtt SAPRotationRole.Arn
      Environment:
        Variables:
          HANA_HOST: !Ref HANAHost
          HANA_PORT: !Ref HANAPort
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical governance basics for a multi-account SAP on AWS setup, focusing on tagging discipline, SCP enforcement, and cross-account access gating with a concrete IaC pattern.

## Key Concepts
- AWS Organizations SCPs and Deny/Allow logic
- AWS resource tagging and Condition keys (aws:RequestTag, aws:ResourceTag)
- IAM role trust and tag-based access control
- PrivateLink and VPC Endpoint Service basics
- Minimal CloudFormation for cross-account roles

## Code Example
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Action": "*",
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {
        "ForAllValues:StringNotEquals": {
          "aws:RequestTag/environment": ["Prod","Shared","DR"],
          "aws:RequestTag/owner": ["sap-admin","ops"]
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["ec2:DescribeInstances","ec2:StartInstances","ec2:StopInstances"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": {
          "aws:ResourceTag/environment": "Prod"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Resources:
  CrossAccountTagGuardRole:
    Type: "AWS::IAM::Role"
    Properties:
      RoleName: "SAPTagGuardRole"
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
        - Effect: "Allow"
          Principal:
            AWS: "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_B:root"
          Action: "sts:AssumeRole"
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: "SAPTagGuard"
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
            - Effect: "Allow"
              Action: "*"
              Resource: "*"
```

## Why This Is Asked

- SAP HANA System Replication (HSR) cross-region
- RPO/RTO trade-offs and latency considerations
- Route 53 health checks and failover

- Cross-region backups with S3 CRR and EBS snapshot copy
- IAM cross-region trust and least privilege

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal IAM cross-region role (illustrative)
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  SAPDRCrossRegionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: SAPDRCrossRegionRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: [ec2.amazonaws.com, ssm.amazonaws.com]
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SAPDRPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: ['ec2:*','s3:*','route53:*','logs:*','ssm:*']
```
